input.rationale: First product of a fresh run: a sourced partial map of hashicorp/raft that establishes both core relationships and their connection. Formation/advancement (A1) is traced from Apply/ApplyLog through leader dispatchLogs, follower appendEntries, commitment.match/recalculate and processLogs application. Context/authority (A2) is traced through StableStore-backed term/vote persistence, the candidate election path, higher-term step-down and the leader lease. The connection is the commitment startIndex gate (a leader may only advance the commit index once a quorum has stored the first entry of its own term) together with the voter-set basis for quorum and the ErrLeadershipLost cleanup of inflight futures on step down. The core_overview is usable; the leadership-transfer handshake, the pipelined append path, user snapshot restore and startup reconstruction remain explicit open details and sourced surfaces rather than claimed coverage.

result.summary: Resubmitted the first-turn product (the prior attempt was rejected only because the final response was not the required JSON envelope, not for content). submission.json is action=research with map_path=maps/core-v1.json and 31 SourceRange citations into the captured hashicorp/raft snapshot; preflight returned valid:true. The map records all seven Activities with applicability and a usable core_overview: A1 formation/advancement (B-leader-dispatch -> B-follower-append -> B-quorum-commit -> B-leader-apply, plus B-commit-term-rule) and A2 context/authority (B-term-vote-persist, B-election, B-authority-loss, B-leader-lease), connected by the commitment startIndex gate (a leader may advance commitIndex only once a quorum stores the first entry of its own term), the voter-set basis of quorum, and ErrLeadershipLost cleanup of inflight futures on step down while the durable log prefix is preserved. Four Facts (F-log-persisted, F-committed, F-term-vote, F-leadership), supporting behaviors for membership eligibility, snapshot recovery and the client API, and sourced Surfaces for the untraced leadership-transfer handshake, restoreUserSnapshot, VerifyLeader (UNCLASSIFIED_PROTOCOL_RESPONSIBILITY) and the pipelined append path. No defect is claimed yet; this map is the accepted-basis prerequisite for a first Candidate.

after.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement: turn client commands into ordered log entries and advance the commit index only on a quorum of the current voter configuration.
after.realization_summary: Leader dispatchLogs assigns (Index,Term), stores locally and notifies replicators; followers appendEntries validate PrevLog and truncate conflicting suffixes; commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex when a quorum has stored up to an index at or after the leader's startIndex; the leader applies committed entries to the FSM.

after.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority: bind every action to a current term, persist the term and vote, and hand leadership over only on a quorum of votes or an explicit transfer.

after.durability: Not durable by itself on the leader; the durable content is the log entries held by a quorum. commitIndex is recomputed after an election.
after.recovery: A new leader recomputes commitment with a fresh startIndex and must replicate its first term entry to a quorum before committing anything.

formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

open_details: Pre-vote and leadership-transfer interactions are only partially traced (see surfaces).
The pipelined append path and the FSM batch manager are unmapped alternative mechanisms for the same facts.
Startup reconstruction in NewRaft is not read, so recovery of F-term-vote and F-log-persisted across restart is sourced only from the store interfaces.
after.rationale: Both core relationships and their connection are grounded in read source: formation/advancement (leader dispatch, follower append, quorum commitment, application) and context/authority (term and vote persistence, election, authority loss, lease). The connection is the startIndex gate on commitment and the voter-set basis for quorum plus the ErrLeadershipLost cleanup on step down. Local anomalies (pipeline path, transfer path, snapshot restore) are retained as open details and surfaces rather than claimed as resolved.

after.reason: VerifyLeader performs a quorum heartbeat liveness check before serving reads; its responsibility (a read-leadership duty) is not yet assigned to an Activity in this map.
Membership-change admission and configuration log appending are mapped to the configuration/eligibility behavior.
The leadership-transfer handshake (TimeoutNow, candidateFromLeadershipTransfer flag, transfer-timeout handling) is only partially traced; it is not part of the traced formation/context backbone yet.
RPC dispatch and protocol-version admission gate the AppendEntries and vote handlers already mapped.
The user-triggered snapshot restore path (log truncation and lastLog recomputation) is not traced; recovery semantics of the map are limited to log/snapshot reconstruction.
The high-performance pipelined AppendEntries path (and its fallback to the RPC path) was not traced; it is an alternative mechanism for the same F-log-persisted/F-committed facts.

after.system_boundary: github.com/hashicorp/raft (captured snapshot commit c0dc6a0b) - a single Go module implementing the Raft consensus algorithm; the library owns election, log replication, commit advancement, membership and FSM application, while Transport, LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and FSM are caller-supplied interfaces.
protocol_contexts: Leader/follower/candidate state machine driven by the rpcCh, applyCh, configurationChangeCh, verifyCh, userRestoreCh and timers of a single main goroutine
RPC contexts AppendEntries, RequestVote, RequestPreVote, InstallSnapshot and TimeoutNow, gated by checkRPCHeader protocol-version negotiation
Membership contexts: at most one uncommitted configuration; voters vs non-voters vs staging
external_interfaces: FSM (fsm.go) plus the public client API in api.go
ownership: Main goroutine owns raftState.currentTerm/state, configurations, LogStore mutation order and RPC handling
commitment struct owns matchIndexes/commitIndex/startIndex under its own mutex
Replication goroutines own followerReplication.nextIndex, failures and pipeline state
selection_injection: Transport, LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and FSM are injected by the caller via Config; the library does not implement them
variants: Pre-vote may be disabled (Config.PreVoteDisabled); leader lease timeout configurable; protocol versions 0-3
unknowns: Durability guarantees of concrete LogStore/StableStore implementations are the caller's responsibility and are not established by this module
